title: Cap. IV Arg. 9 Sol: Minor — Christ founds more than the general decree; Christianity's true foundations
pass_a_gloss: To answer the Minor in a word suffices; that Christ is the foundation of that general decree concerning whosoever are to be saved under the condition of faith; but not of that alone, but also of other decrees, according to which to singular persons, given by the Father to Christ before the foundations of the world were laid, grace and glory will be gifted in their time. The Remonstrants ought not to have buried these latter decrees under such obstinate silence, and to stick in that first universal one, unless they opine that there never was any decree in the Divine mind concerning singular persons to be imbued with efficacious grace, and by such grace to be led through to glory. Let us go on, and weigh those things which have been brought forward for confirmation of either proposition. They cry that the Major is manifest, because there is no salvation or blessing unto salvation except in Christ. A frivolous proof. Is it because no benefit is decreed to be conferred on us except in Christ, that therefore any decree whatsoever looking to our salvation, whose foundation is Christ, will be our very election itself? This coheres as sand without lime. But they say the Minor also is clear, because that only decree, I will save all Believers, is the foundation of Christianity, of salvation, and of certainty concerning salvation. I answer, that that only general decree is not the foundation of Christianity. For there are other foundations of Christianity, and among others that chief foundation; that Faith and perseverance, and whatever leads infallibly to heaven, are special gifts of special grace, not contingent effects arising from the choice of a man not yet elected, and motives of Divine election.
pass_b_english: On the Minor in a word: Christ is foundation of that general decree to save whosoever under the condition of faith — but not of that alone; also of other decrees by which singular persons, given by the Father to Christ before the world's foundations, will in their time be gifted grace and glory. Remonstrants should not bury those later decrees in obstinate silence and stick in the first universal one, unless they think there never was a decree in God's mind to imbue singular persons with efficacious grace and lead them by it to glory. They cry the Major plain because no salvation except in Christ — a frivolous proof. Because no benefit is decreed for us except in Christ, is every Christ-founded salvation-decree therefore our election itself? That coheres like sand without lime. They say the Minor is clear because I will save all Believers founds Christianity, salvation, and certainty. I answer: that general decree alone is not Christianity's foundation. There are others — chief among them that faith, perseverance, and whatever leads infallibly to heaven are special gifts of special grace, not contingent effects from the choice of a man not yet elected, and motives of divine election.
source_text: Ad Minorem verbo respondere sufficit; Christum esse fundamentum generalis ejus decreti de salvandis quibuscunque sub conditione fidei; sed non ejus solius, verum etiam aliorum decretorum, secundum quae singularibus personis, Christo a Patre datis ante jacta mundi fundamenta, gratia et gloria suo tempore donabitur. Non debuerunt Remonstrantes tam obstinato silentio obruere haec posteriora decreta, et in illo primo universali haerere, nisi opinentur nullum unquam fuisse decretum in mente Divina de singularibus personis efficaci gratia imbuendis, et per talem gratiam ad gloriam perducendis. Pergamus, et ea pensitemus quae ad confirmationem utriusque propositionis adducta sunt. Majorem clamant esse manifestam, quia nulla est salus vel benedictio ad salutem nisi in Christo. Frivola probatio. An quia nullum beneficium decernitur in nos conferendum nisi in Christo, idcirco quodlibet decretum ad salutem nostram spectans, cujus fundamentum est Christus, erit ipsissima nostra electio? Tam hoc cohaeret quam arena sine calce. Sed Minorem perspicuam etiam esse dicunt, quia illud unicum decretum, Ego salvabo omnes Credentes, est fundamentum Christianismi, salutis, et certitudinis de salute. Respondeo, illud unicum decretum generale non esse fundamentum Christianismi. Sunt enim alia Christianismi fundamenta, et inter alia illud praecipuum fundamentum; Fidem et perseverantiam, ac quicquid ad caelum ducit infallibiliter, esse specialia specialis gratiae dona, non autem contingentia effecta ex arbitrio hominis nondum electi nascentia, et electionis Divinae motiva.
